functions.name: AnalyzeFontTextureSheet32
functions.summary: 32-bit RGBA font texture sheet analyzer. Locks the texture surface via ThunkWithArgReorder, derives horizontal/vertical cell divisions by scanning the pixel buffer for key-color sentinels, builds a per-cell glyph lookup table at this+0x6D, then rewrites every pixel: key colors become 0xF0F0F0 with the surface modification flag set, non-key pixels get forced alpha 0xFF000000. Stores the default key color at this+0x2C and unlocks the surface via ArgumentReorderWrapper_3230.

operations.description: Lock the texture surface: call ThunkWithArgReorder with the surface pointer stored at this+0x64 and its pixel-data pointer at surface+0x18; the returned buffer is the locked pixel array.
Read the locked surface dimensions used for all cell arithmetic: width at surface+0x1C, height at surface+0x20 and row pitch at surface+0x28.
Recover the three key-color sentinels from the tail of the pixel buffer (the sentinel row written after the glyph grid) and store them at this+0x28, this+0x2C and this+0x30.
Scan the pixel buffer along the row stride looking for the first pixel equal to the key color at this+0x28; the scan distance yields the horizontal cell count, stored at this+0x34.
Derive the horizontal cell pitch as the surface width (surface+0x1C) divided by the horizontal cell count and store it at this+0x3C.
Scan the pixel buffer along the pitch stride (surface+0x28) looking for the next key-color pixel; the scan distance yields the vertical cell count, stored at this+0x38.

Derive the vertical cell pitch as the surface height (surface+0x20) divided by the vertical cell count and store it at this+0x40; compute the total cell count plus 32 overhead entries and store it at this+0x44.

For every cell, resolve the glyph pixel index by walking the column/row strides and matching the key color; write the 8-byte cell metadata record at this+0x6D (u/v stride indices plus glyph index), advancing 8 bytes per cell.

Rewrite every pixel (width x height): if it equals one of the three key colors (this+0x28, this+0x2C, this+0x30) set it to 15790320 (0xF0F0F0) and OR the surface modification flag at surface+0x18 with 0x800; otherwise force the alpha channel by ORing the pixel with 0xFF000000.
Store the default key color 15790320 (0xF0F0F0) into this+0x2C as the canonical transparency color.
Unlock the surface by returning the result of ArgumentReorderWrapper_3230 called with the same surface pointer (this+0x64) and pixel-data pointer arguments.

unresolved: The exact semantics of the 8-byte cell metadata record fields (glyph index, u/v stride positions) are inferred from the write pattern, not confirmed against a glyph consumer.
Caller TexturePathParsingAndDimensionCalculation (0x00552F20) determines when the 32-bit variant is used; the relationship to the 8-bit/other-format analyzers is not established here.

functions.name: LinePolygonRasterizer
functions.summary: Bresenham-style line/polygon rasterizer. Selects a pixel-format conversion (RGB555, RGB565 or direct color) from a6[12], then chooses a 16-bit or 32-bit fill pipeline from a6[9]. Computes horizontal and vertical extents between two endpoints (a1,a2)-(a3,a4); zero-extent cases draw a single vertical or horizontal span, and diagonal cases run error-term driven fills through the selected fill functions with a per-row stride derived from a6[10].

operations.description: Read pixel-format selector v6 = a6[12] and cache v7 = a5.
If v6 == 6 convert the packed color a5 to RGB555: v9 = ((a5 >> 3) & 0x1F) + ((a5 >> 5) & 0x7E0) + ((a5 >> 8) & 0xF800).
Otherwise v9 = a4: the caller-supplied color value is used directly.
Retrieve the destination surface v24 = ThunkWithArgReorder(a6, 0, 0).
If a6[9] == 16 select the 16-bit fill pipeline.

16-bit pipeline: v26 = ClampedPixelSpanFill, v25 = sub_553D00, v27 = F_16BitPixelRectangleFill, v29 = PixelFillWithStrideStepCalculation; per-row stride v10 = (int)a6[10] >> 1 and shift amount v11 = 1.
32-bit pipeline: v26 = sub_553D40, v25 = DrawRectangle, v27 = F_2DArrayFillWithStrideSupport, v29 = NestedLoopArrayFillWithStride; stride v10 = (int)a6[10] >> 2 and shift amount v11 = 2.
Horizontal extent v13 = abs32(a3 - a1).
If v13 == 0 the endpoints share a column: draw a vertical span through v25 with the converted color and stride, then return ArgumentReorderWrapper_3230(a6, 0, 0).
Vertical extent v14 = abs32(a4 - a2).
If v14 == 0 the endpoints share a row: draw a horizontal span through v26 with the converted color and stride, then return ArgumentReorderWrapper_3230(a6, 0, 0).

Steep branch (v13 >= v14): compute error terms v15 = v14 << v11 and v16/v30 = (v14 - v13) << v11; pick the start pixel from (a1,a2) or (a3,a4) depending on the slope direction and optionally negate the stride v10.
Fill the steep diagonal line via v27 with the span parameters, run length, color and stride.
Shallow branch (v13 < v14): compute error terms v18 = v13 << v11 and v28/v31 = (v13 - v14) << v11; choose the start pixel by comparing a2 against a4 and a3 against a1.
Fill the shallow diagonal line via v29 with span parameters, direction (2 * v20 - 1), stride and color.
Both diagonal paths finish by returning ArgumentReorderWrapper_3230(a6, 0, 0).
